# tests/test_is_valid_email.py
import pytest

from your_module import is_valid_email  # TODO: replace with the module containing the function


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "email",
    [
        "user@example.com",
        "USER@EXAMPLE.COM",
        "first.last@example.com",
        "first_last@example.com",
        "name+tag@example.co.uk",
        "name-tag%filter@example-domain.org",
        "a@b.co",  # minimal valid local/domain/TLD lengths for this regex
        "user@example.museum",  # long TLD
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_accepts_valid_emails(email: str) -> None:
    assert is_valid_email(email) is True


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "email",
    [
        "",
        "plainaddress",
        "@example.com",
        "user@",
        "user@example",
        "user@example.",
        "user@example.c",       # TLD too short
        "user@example.123",     # numeric TLD
        "user@example.c0m",     # digit in TLD
        "user@@example.com",
        "user name@example.com",
        "user@example .com",
        "user@exa_mple.com",    # underscore not allowed in domain by this regex
        "user@example,com",
        " user@example.com",
        "user@example.com ",
        "\tuser@example.com",
        "user@example.com\t",
        "line\nbreak@example.com",
        "üser@example.com",     # non-ASCII local part not supported by this regex
        "user@exämple.com",     # non-ASCII domain not supported by this regex
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_rejects_invalid_emails(email: str) -> None:
    assert is_valid_email(email) is False


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "email",
    [
        None,
        123,
        12.3,
        True,
        [],
        {},
        b"user@example.com",
    ],
)
def test_is_valid_email_raises_type_error_for_non_string_inputs(email: object) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        is_valid_email(email)  # type: ignore[arg-type]


# Optional edge-case test documenting a current implementation quirk:

@pytest.mark.xfail(reason="Current implementation accepts a final newline because it uses re.match + '$'.")
def test_is_valid_email_rejects_trailing_newline() -> None:
    assert is_valid_email("user@example.com\n") is False
